chunk_a.text_snippet:
Title: Denmark’s King Frederik and Queen Mary to visit Australia – as it happened
Date: 2026-01-30

Content: It means the Nationals effectively have nine days to reconcile with the Liberals before Ley appoints a permanent, Liberal-only frontbench. In a statement, Ley said: There is enormous talent in the parliamentary Liberal party and my party room is more than capable of permanently fulfilling each and every one of those roles. Equally, the Nationals’ decision to leave the Coalition was both regrettable and unnecessary and that door remains open. The Liberal and National parties exist to serve the Australian people and the maintenance of a strong and functioning relationship between both is in the national interest — whether we are in a formal Coalition or not. Guardian Australia this week reported Ley wanted to meet David Littleproud for last-minute talks on the future of the Coalition ahead of parliament’s return, but the Nationals leader rebuffed the invitation to focus on a leadership spill scheduled for Monday afternoon.

chunk_b.text_snippet:
Title: Palestine Action Group plans ‘national day of protest’ as Herzog visit confirmed – as it happened
Date: 2026-01-28

Content: In the message, obtained by Guardian Australia, Ley said: I reminded him that as the leaders of the Liberal and National parties, we are the stewards of two great movements that exist to serve the Australian people and that maintaining a strong and functioning relationship between our two parties is in the national interest – whether in formal Coalition or not. Ley said Littleproud rejected the offer as he prepares to face a motion to spill the leadership from disgruntled backbencher Colin Boyce at next Monday’s party room meeting. The note to MPs continued: David’s team have just advised mine that his focus is the spill motion he now faces and he is therefore unavailable to meet until after that spill is considered. The leadership of The Nationals is a matter for their party room to determine. We will talk to whoever The Nationals elect as their leader, because whether we are in a Coalition or not, it is our responsibility to hold the Albanese Government to account.

t_bridge: Littleproud's leadership spill and Ley's Coalition reconciliation attempts.

initial_question.rag_input: Why did David Littleproud turn down Sussan Ley’s request for talks regarding the Liberal-National Coalition ahead of the 30 January 2026 return of parliament?
initial_question.question: Why did David Littleproud turn down Sussan Ley’s request for talks regarding the Liberal-National Coalition ahead of the 30 January 2026 return of parliament?
initial_question.answer: David Littleproud rebuffed Sussan Ley’s invitation for last-minute talks on the future of the Coalition because he was focused on preparing for a leadership spill motion initiated by backbencher Colin Boyce, which was scheduled for the afternoon of Monday, 2 February 2026.
